newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel warns Arafat against police violence.
newsitem.headline: Israel warns Arafat against police violence.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority in remarks broadcast on Friday against using policemen "as instruments of murder" aimed at Israelis.
Israel's army arrested three Palestinian police officers in the West Bank on Monday, announcing it had thwarted an attack on Jews at a settlement near Nablus.

"We cannot accept the violence as a principle of negotiations...and certainly not the use of Palestinian policemen as instruments of murder against Israeli citizens," Netanyahu said in broadcast remarks.
Israel has demanded Arafat act against the officers and any others involved. Arafat rejected Israeli allegations of possible involvement by senior Palestinian officials.
"It's part of a comprehensive campaign launched by the Israelis against the Palestinian Authority," Arafat told reporters in self-ruled Ramallah after his weekly cabinet meeting on Friday night.

Netanyahu sent his Shin Bet security chief Ami Ayalon to Gaza on Thursday to press the point. Ayalon handed Arafat the videotaped confession of one of the police officers, said Palestinian senior official Nabil Shaath.

"We received the videotape of the so-called confession of this person. We are taking it very seriously. We are investigating very seriously and we demanded that the three soldiers (policemen) be handed over to us," Shaath told Channel Two television.
Shaath, who said all three police officers had confessed, called the information "not solid", saying it was unclear under what condition the confessions were made.

Israeli security sources said Arafat had appointed a commission on Friday to probe the allegations. Palestinian security chief Nasr Yousef told Reuters: "There was something in that direction but no decision."

Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper, quoting Israeli security sources, said a PLO police chief was behind the attempted shooting attack, hoping an escalation in violence would break a four-month-old peacemaking deadlock over the start of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
"It appears operating the cell was supposed to bring about an escalation in relations between Israel and the Palestinian Authority that would break the impasse in negotiations," the newspaper said.
Earlier in the week the Palestinian governor of Nablus, Mahmoud al-Alloul, said Israeli allegations about PLO police plotting an attack on Jews were "absolutely untrue".
Palestinian police operate in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip under Israel-PLO peace deals reached since 1993.

Security cooperation between Israeli and Palestinian troops outlined in the deals has broken down since the March deadlock with the Jewish state accusing Arafat's administration of stirring anti-Israel riots in Hebron and other West Bank towns.
Mediators have tried in recent months to revive peacemaking, among them the European Union's special Middle East envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos who was expected back in Israel on Sunday.
"He will be back on Sunday, probably for more meetings with the two leaders," said Moratinos' adviser Christophe Farnaud.
